newsitem.title: USA: CSCE AND NYCE RETAIN JP MORGAN AS MERGER ADVISOR.
newsitem.headline: CSCE AND NYCE RETAIN JP MORGAN AS MERGER ADVISOR.

text.p: The New York Cotton Exchange (NYCE) and the Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange (CSCE) said on Thursday that they have jointly agreed to retain J.P. Morgan & Co Inc to act as a facilitator in ongoing merger discussions between the two exchanges.
In June of 1997, NYCE and CSCE announced their agreement to explore the possibility of a merger.
The chairmen and presidents of both exchanges were instructed to develop a merger proposal which would be equitable to the members of each exchange.

"J.P. Morgan's role will be to focus on the proposed design of a merger proposal to obtain the support of the memberships of the two exchanges, and will include an analysis of the present and future outlook of the two exchanges and the potential benefits of a combination," the CSCE and NYCE said in a joint statement.
The exchanges said a CSCE-NYCE merger would be expected to result in cost efficiences benefiting members and other market users.

Additionally, the merger of the two exchanges would strengthen their ability to continue to offer efficient and liquid markets in a variety of agricultural and finiancial products, the exchanges said.
Previously the two exchanges said they planned to build a joint trading facility in lower Manhattan, although no work had begun on the site.
There have also been discussions about the CSCE and NYCE moving to the new New York Mercantile Exchange facility.
The CSCE lists futures and options contracts in coffee, cocoa, sugar and dairy products.
The NYCE lists futures and options contracts in cotton, orange juice and financial futures including the U.S. Dollar Index, treasury notes and U.S.-based currency contracts.
